correctness.rationale: The source gives the unique root \(\nu(\rho)\), the endpoint bound \(p=1-\nu(\rho)=O(\varepsilon^2)\), the positive value \(J_0=I_\mu(1,1)\), and bounded \(I_{\mu\mu}\). Directly, \(I(1,1-\varepsilon)=1-\cos(\pi\varepsilon)\) and \(I_{\mu\rho}(1,1)=-\pi\operatorname{Si}(2\pi)\). Taylor expansion in \(\mu\) therefore has remainder \(O(p^2)=O(\varepsilon^4)\), yielding the stated quadratic and cubic coefficients with all signs and normalizations checked.

value.rationale: The function \(\nu(\rho)\) is the exact sharp parameter of the newly solved all-parameter conjecture, and the source devotes a separate endpoint argument to bounding its deficit by nearby quadratic multiples. Replacing that bracket by an exact tangency coefficient and identifying the first cubic correction gives the local geometry of the sharp threshold itself. This is a natural structural refinement of the main optimal parameter curve, not an arbitrary finite computation or cosmetic tightening.
